system_description.narrative_title: Global bond-market rout and rising yields, with France as focal contagion
system_description.narrative_summary: Across this news window the single dominant narrative is a global bond-market rout — sharply rising sovereign and corporate yields that are re-pricing risk, pressuring equities, prompting central bank scrutiny and reshaping investor flows. Treasuries, gilts and euro-area bonds are feeding back into sovereign credit stress (notably France), FX moves and commodity demand, while policy signals (Fed minutes, central-bank commentary) and on-the-ground events (French protests, fiscal plans) act as external inputs and catalysts in an open system of capital flows, expectations and fiscal/financial stability feedback loops.
system_description.scope: Global fixed-income markets (sovereign and corporate yields), major central-bank policy signals (Fed, ECB, BoJ, Bank of France), key sovereign fiscal positions (especially France), market participants (investors, bond vigilantes, quant funds), and immediate cross-market spillovers (equities, FX, gold, auctions).
system_description.super_system: The global financial system and macroeconomic environment (monetary policy regime, international capital flows, global growth/inflation dynamics).
adjacent_subsystems: Sovereign fiscal policy and political stability (e.g., France's budget and protests)
Equity and corporate debt markets (issuance, LBOs, corporate credit risk)
Foreign exchange and commodity markets (dollar strength, gold, oil)
evidence_headlines: Investors see big opportunity in ferocious 2026 bond-market rout
Global bond sell-off resumes as 30-year Treasury yield hits highest since 2002
France Is Discovering the Cost of Higher Yields
France is caught between angry students and unforgiving bond markets
Fed officials see another hike coming, but no sign as to when, minutes show
Bond Vigilantes Find New Reasons to Worry

variables.name: Long-term sovereign yield level
variables.description: The prevailing market yield on long-maturity government debt instruments, measured as a continuous average for benchmark long-dated issues.

variables.name: Sovereign credit spread level
variables.description: The market-implied premium investors demand over benchmark yields for a given sovereign, measured as a continuous spread reflecting perceived sovereign credit risk.

variables.name: Corporate credit spread level
variables.description: The average premium that corporate bond yields trade above sovereign or benchmark yields, capturing continuously varying corporate credit risk and risk appetite.

variables.name: Bond market liquidity
variables.description: The continuous ease and depth with which fixed-income instruments can be transacted without large price impact, measured by bid-ask spreads, market depth and immediacy.

variables.name: Bond yield volatility
variables.description: The short- to medium-term variability of bond yields as a continuous measure of price movement risk in fixed-income markets.

variables.name: Term premium
variables.description: The component of long-term yields attributable to compensation for holding duration risk over shorter-term yields, varying continuously with investor risk tolerance and uncertainty.

variables.name: Inflation expectations
variables.description: Market and investor consensus about future inflation rates over specified horizons, measured as a continuously varying expectation metric.

variables.name: Monetary policy path expectations
variables.description: Market-implied expectations of the future trajectory of policy tightening or easing, represented continuously by forward rate probabilities and pricing.

variables.name: Sovereign fiscal financing need
variables.description: The ongoing magnitude of a sovereign's expected debt issuance and refinancing requirement relative to market capacity, expressed as a continuous stress variable.

variables.name: Sovereign debt durational exposure
variables.description: The aggregated sensitivity of a sovereign's debt stock to changes in yields, measured continuously by average maturity and interest rate repricing profile.

variables.name: Cross‑asset capital flow rate
variables.description: The net continuous flow of capital between major asset classes (bonds, equities, FX, commodities) driven by relative returns and risk re-pricing.

variables.name: Equity market valuation pressure
variables.description: The continuous degree to which equity prices are under upward or downward pressure from changes in discount rates, earnings expectations and asset substitution.

variables.name: Currency adjustment pressure
variables.description: The continuous stress on exchange rates arising from interest rate differentials, capital flows and market re-pricing, measured as directional pressure and realized moves.

variables.name: Safe‑asset demand
variables.description: The continuous level of investor preference for low-risk, high-liquidity assets (e.g., high-quality government debt and gold) as a function of risk aversion and uncertainty.

variables.name: Market leverage and margin pressure
variables.description: The continuous build-up and unwind pressure from leveraged positions and margin requirements in fixed-income and related markets, affecting liquidity and forced selling risk.

variables.name: Auction absorption capacity
variables.description: The continuous ability of capital markets to absorb sovereign and corporate debt issuance at prevailing yields without materially disrupting price discovery.

catalysts.title: France willing to bypass parliament to pass cuts
catalysts.description: French government readiness to bypass parliament to push through large spending cuts could materially alter market perceptions of France's fiscal trajectory and immediate financing needs.
catalysts.rationale: "French Government Is Willing to Bypass Parliament to Pass Billions in Cuts"; could lower perceived fiscal risk, narrowing spreads.

catalysts.title: France considers more short-term debt issuance
catalysts.description: Policy shift toward issuing a larger share of shorter-term paper to soothe the long-end after the rout, changing duration profile and auction cadence.
catalysts.rationale: "France Considers Issuing More Shorter-Term Debt After Bond-Market Turmoil" — short issuance reduces duration but stresses auctions.

catalysts.title: Debate/decision on pausing ECB quantitative tightening
catalysts.description: Market and policy debate could lead the ECB to pause QT or adjust its balance-sheet path, shifting policy expectations and liquidity conditions across euro bonds.
catalysts.rationale: "Bond turbulence means it’s time for the ECB to put QT on hold" and debate cited by Bank of France headlines.

catalysts.title: Additional Fed rate hike expected later this year
catalysts.description: Fed minutes imply another rate increase this year is possible; a further hike would reshape global policy expectations and push yields higher.
catalysts.rationale: "Fed Minutes Signal Further Rate Increase This Year" and officials saw another hike coming, affecting global yields and demand.

catalysts.title: Upcoming large sovereign bond auctions (US, Europe)
catalysts.description: A sequence of large benchmark auctions in the US and Europe will test market absorption; weak demand could widen yields and strain liquidity.
catalysts.rationale: "Auction Action Calms Treasurys" and strong/weak auctions directly influence absorption and yields.

catalysts.title: Escalation of student and broader protests in France
catalysts.description: Ongoing and intensifying protests raise political risk, could complicate fiscal consolidation and unsettle bond markets and the euro.
catalysts.rationale: "Student riots engulf France" and "School protests sweeping France" raise political/fiscal risk, pressuring spreads and euro.

catalysts.title: Japanese funds reduce exposure to French sovereigns
catalysts.description: Portfolio reallocation by Japanese bond desks away from French paper could create cross-border outflows, reducing auction demand and widening spreads.
catalysts.rationale: "Tokyo Bond Desks Say Sayonara as Japan Reconsiders Its French Love Affair" — potential Japanese outflows from French bonds.

catalysts.title: Leveraged unwind / margin stress in bond market
catalysts.description: Rising yields could trigger margin calls and forced selling by leveraged players, reducing liquidity and amplifying yield moves and volatility.
catalysts.rationale: "Investors see big opportunity in ferocious 2026 bond-market rout"; Fed minutes note preparing for market stress.
